key_terms.meaning: A calibrated oscillator, amplifier, attenuator and headphone set that presents pure tones of known frequency and known loudness to one ear at a time.
0 dB HL is the median threshold of hearing of healthy young ears at that frequency; a reading of 40 dB HL means the tone had to be 40 dB louder than normal.
Threshold search at octave or half-octave frequencies from 125 Hz to 8 kHz by the Hughson-Westlake method: 10 dB down after a response, 5 dB up after no response.
Tone delivered by a vibrator pressed on the mastoid, bypassing the outer and middle ear, so it tests the inner ear and nerve only.

Same machine, spoken words instead of tones: speech reception threshold is the level of 50 % correct word detection, and the discrimination score is the % of words repeated correctly at comfortable loudness.
A tube of fibres or a camera on a cable that carries light into a body cavity and an image back to the eye or a monitor.
A bundle in which the two ends are fused so that every fibre keeps the same place at both ends; only then is the pixel pattern of the image preserved.
Many unarranged glass fibres that only deliver illumination to the tip; order does not matter because no image travels through them.
The pointed lead-lined tube on a dental X-ray head that limits the beam to about 60 mm at the patient's skin.
Current that enters and leaves through the skin, so most of the voltage is dropped across the dry outer layer and the current is limited to milliamperes.
Current carried straight to the heart by a catheter, pacemaker lead or saline-filled tube, so skin resistance is bypassed and tens of microamperes are enough.
Current that flows from live parts to earth through insulation or capacitance rather than through the intended circuit; at 50 Hz it is measured with a low-resistance ammeter to earth.
Passing a known current (about 25 A) between the earth pin of the plug and exposed metal, and confirming the resistance is small (a fraction of an ohm).
Applying 500 V DC between live parts and the chassis or earth and confirming the resistance is very high (of the order of megohms), proving the insulation is dry and intact.
The band (A/B/C/D in India, I/IIa/IIb/III in Europe, I/II/III in the USA) that a regulator gives a device from its intended use and hazards; the class fixes the evidence and licence needed.
The transient fall in skin resistance that follows sweating after an arousing stimulus, recorded as a small wave on a chart.
The steady resistance of the skin at rest, mostly set by the moisture of the outer layer, typically in the hundreds of kilohms on the palm.
Instrument that measures eye pressure from the force needed to flatten a fixed area of cornea, using P = F/A.
A slit illuminator plus a stereo microscope that cuts an optical section through the transparent eye so each layer can be seen in depth.
Instrument that projects an infrared pattern onto the retina, measures the reflected image, and prints the sphere, cylinder and axis in dioptres.

takeaways: A pure-tone audiometer does one job: it finds the softest tone a person can hear at each frequency, and the answer is written in dB HL with 0 dB set to the normal ear.
The audiogram separates conductive loss from nerve loss by comparing air conduction with bone conduction; a gap between them means the outer or middle ear is at fault.
An endoscope needs one bundle to carry light in and a second, ordered bundle (or a camera chip) to carry the image out; if the image fibres lose their order, the picture becomes a blur of light.
A dental X-ray set uses low kVp, a small focal spot, a narrow collimator cone and a short exposure, so the dose per film is a few microsieverts.
Tissue is damaged by current, not by voltage; dry skin makes the body a poor conductor, but a catheter to the heart removes that protection.
Macroshock needs tens of milliamperes to fibrillate the heart, while microshock can do it with tens of microamperes, which is why cardiac-connected equipment has the tightest leakage limits.
Electrical safety rests on three defences, earthing, isolation and double insulation, and is verified by four tests, inspection, earth continuity, insulation resistance and leakage current.
A device's risk class decides its regulatory path: the higher the class, the more bench data, animal or clinical evidence and third-party audit it needs before a licence.
A polygraph records skin resistance, breathing and pulse together and marks the moment of each question; it measures arousal, not truth, and courts treat it with caution.

Each ophthalmic instrument produces one number: the tonometer gives pressure in mmHg, the auto refractometer gives lens power in dioptres, and the slit lamp gives a magnified optical section rather than a number.
bank_note: Long answers here are mostly 'principle, block diagram, working, specification, limitation', with the electrical safety question usually asked as a comparison of macroshock and microshock and the tests used to prove safety.

bank.q: Draw the block diagram of a pure-tone audiometer and explain how a hearing level in dB HL is defined, produced and plotted on an audiogram.
outline: Oscillator with frequency selection 125 Hz to 8 kHz
Amplifier, step attenuator in 5 dB steps, interrupter switch
Calibrated earphone and bone vibrator
0 dB HL = median threshold of normal ears, calibrated against reference equivalent threshold SPL
Audiogram: frequency on a log x-axis, dB HL on an inverted y-axis
Symbols O and X for right and left air conduction, < and > for bone conduction
Hughson-Westlake staircase procedure and masking of the non-test ear

bank.q: Describe the construction and working of a flexible fibre-optic endoscope. Explain why the image bundle must be coherent while the light bundle need not be.
outline: Two bundles: light guide and image guide
Core and cladding of each fibre, total internal reflection
Fibre diameter of the order of 10 to 30 micrometres; thousands of fibres
Objective lens at the tip, eyepiece or camera coupler at the other end
Coherent bundle keeps the same fibre order at both ends, so it carries a pixel map of the image
Incoherent bundle only delivers light to the cavity
Air and water channels, bending section, deflection controls, light source and insufflation

bank.q: Explain macroshock and microshock. Give the current thresholds for perception, let-go, respiratory tetany and ventricular fibrillation, and state the leakage limits for cardiac-connected equipment.
outline: Injury depends on current density and path, not on voltage
Body resistance: dry skin about 10 to 100 kilohm, internal tissue a few hundred ohm
Perception about 1 mA, let-go about 10 to 16 mA, respiratory tetany 20 to 30 mA, fibrillation 75 to 100 mA at 50 Hz
Microshock: conductor inside the heart, skin resistance bypassed, fibrillation possible at tens of microamperes
Microshock pathways: saline-filled catheter, pacemaker lead, wet electrode, earthed plumbing
Limits: patient leakage current about 10 microampere for type CF, 100 microampere for type BF, earth leakage a few hundred microampere for Class I

bank.q: List and explain the four tests used to verify the electrical safety of a medical equipment installation.
outline: Visual inspection: plug, cord, fuse rating, labels, battery, no cracks
Earth continuity: about 25 A injected between earth pin and exposed metal, resistance well under 1 ohm
Insulation resistance: 500 V DC between live parts and chassis or earth, resistance in the megohm range
Leakage current: equipment connected to supply with the leads in a safety analyser, earth leakage, enclosure leakage and patient leakage measured in normal and single-fault condition
Accept and reject values with reference to the applicable standard
Records and repeat test intervals

bank.q: Explain how a polygraph records galvanic skin response, respiration and pulse. Define basal skin resistance and say why all channels are recorded together.
outline: GSR: two electrodes on palm or fingers, a small constant current or voltage, resistance or conductance recorded
Basal skin resistance is the resting value, hundreds of kilohm on the palm
An arousing stimulus triggers sweat secretion and resistance falls, giving a wave
Respiration by a chest and an abdominal belt, pneumograph or strain gauge
Cardiovascular channel by cuff or photoplethysmograph
Marker pen or digital event mark at the instant each question is asked
Why together: arousal appears in several channels at different delays, and the marker separates stimulus from response

bank.q: An audiogram shows air conduction of 40 dB HL and bone conduction of 10 dB HL at 2 kHz in one ear, with normal readings at 250 Hz. Interpret the result, name the type of loss and state where the defect lies.
outline: Air-bone gap of 30 dB at 2 kHz
Bone conduction near normal means the inner ear and nerve work
Gap means the outer or middle ear blocks air-conducted sound
Diagnosis: conductive hearing loss, here mild to moderate at 2 kHz
Possible causes: wax, effusion, otosclerosis, perforation
Next steps: otoscopy, tympanometry, repeat with masking to rule out cross-hearing

bank.q: A technician tests a Class I patient monitor in an ICU and records earth continuity of 0.8 ohm, insulation resistance of 0.5 megohm and earth leakage current of 300 microampere. Decide which results pass, and state what protection a patient with a pacemaker needs.
outline: Earth continuity 0.8 ohm is too high for a protective earth, so this fails
Insulation resistance 0.5 megohm is far below the expected megohm values, so this fails
Earth leakage 300 microampere may be under the usual few-hundred microampere limit for Class I but must be read with the standard
Any single failure means the unit is withdrawn and repaired
Pacemaker patient needs type CF, cardiac-floating, applied part
Patient leakage limit about 10 microampere; isolated input, battery operation where possible
Equipotential bonding, no unearthed metal near the bed, earth-free zone for intracardiac procedures

bank.q: Describe a dental X-ray machine and list the practical steps that keep the patient's dose low during an intraoral exposure.
outline: Tube: tungsten anode, thermionic filament, evacuated glass envelope, oil and lead housing
Settings of the order of 60 to 70 kVp and a few milliampere, exposure of a fraction of a second
Small focal spot, short cone or open-ended spacer, collimation to about 60 mm at the skin
Aluminium filtration to remove soft X-rays

Steps: correct film or sensor, fast film or digital, lead apron and thyroid collar, beam-aiming with the patient still, avoid retakes, hold film by holder not by finger, staff behind shield, badge monitoring
Dose per intraoral film is a few microsieverts; ALARA principle

bank.q: An auto refractometer prints -2.00 D sphere, -0.75 D cylinder, axis 180 degrees for the right eye. Explain what each number means and how the instrument obtained them.
outline: Dioptre is the reciprocal of focal length in metres
Negative sphere means myopia, the eye is too powerful or too long
Cylinder is the extra power in one meridian, axis is its direction in degrees
Instrument projects an infrared ring or pattern onto the retina and measures the size and shape of the reflected image
Spherical error shifts focus, astigmatism distorts the image into an ellipse
Internal computation averages several readings and gives vertex distance and pupillary distance
Purpose: quick objective starting point before subjective refraction

bank.q: Compare the electrical safety design of an ECG machine used in a general ward with one used in a cardiac catheterisation laboratory. Justify each difference.
outline: Ward: intact skin, macroshock is the main risk, type BF or Class I with protective earth is acceptable
Cath lab: catheter or guide wire inside the heart, microshock dominates
Type CF applied part, patient leakage current of the order of 10 microampere
Isolation of the patient circuit by transformer, optocoupler or battery operation
Earth-free zone or equipotential bonding of all metal near the table
Single-fault condition testing, no earthed metal within reach of the patient
Defibrillation-proof inputs because a defibrillator is used in the same room

bank.q: A start-up has built a new pulse oximeter. Trace the route from working prototype to legal sale in India, and explain how a change of risk class changes the evidence demanded.
outline: Fix the intended use and the risk class under the national medical device rules, class A to D in India
Quality management system, generally ISO 13485, and risk management to ISO 14971
Bench tests: electrical safety to IEC 60601-1 and its particular standard, electromagnetic compatibility, performance and accuracy of SpO2
Biocompatibility of the sensor, software validation, shelf life and sterilisation if applicable
Clinical evidence or literature for the claims, more for higher classes
Application to the central authority, plant inspection, grant of manufacturing licence, labelling and unique device identification
Post-market surveillance, complaint handling and adverse event reporting, and re-evaluation if the intended use widens into a higher class

bank.q: A polygraph record shows a large GSR wave to the fourth question, no change in breathing and a small rise in pulse. Evaluate how much weight this deserves and identify the sources of error.
outline: Polygraph measures arousal, not deception
GSR is the most sensitive and fastest channel but also the least specific
Single channel response has no diagnostic value on its own
Order effects and habituation; the question before may carry over
Artefacts: movement, deep breath, cough, dry electrodes, loose cuff, room temperature, sweat from fear of the test itself
Countermeasures by the subject: biting the tongue, tensing muscles, mental arithmetic
Legal position in India: results without consent are not admissible as evidence; consent and expert interpretation needed

bank.q: Compare Goldmann applanation tonometry with Schiotz indentation tonometry, and state which is preferred for a mass glaucoma screening camp and why.
outline: Both use force over an area; normal intraocular pressure is roughly 10 to 21 mmHg
Goldmann: flattens a fixed 3.06 mm diameter area, force read with a slit lamp, fluorescein and cobalt blue light, Imbert-Fick assumption
Schiotz: weighted plunger indents the cornea, deflection read on a scale and converted by a calibration chart
Goldmann: more accurate, less affected by corneal stiffness, needs slit lamp, anaesthetic and trained operator
Schiotz: portable and cheap but dependent on corneal rigidity and calibration
Screening choice: non-contact air-puff or portable rebound tonometer when many people must be seen quickly, with abnormal cases referred for Goldmann
Confounders: corneal thickness, astigmatism, pressure on the lid

glossary.def: A graph of hearing threshold in dB HL against frequency in hertz, drawn separately for each ear.
The difference in dB between air-conduction and bone-conduction thresholds at one frequency; a gap points to a conductive loss.
A noise presented to the non-test ear so that a loud tone in the test ear is not heard by the other cochlea.
Light travelling in a fibre core strikes the cladding at a shallow angle and is reflected back completely, so it stays inside the fibre.
The hollow tube running the length of a flexible endoscope through which biopsy forceps, snares or suction are passed.
An endoscope with a small solid-state camera chip at the tip instead of an image bundle, sending a video signal up the cable.
The small area on the X-ray anode where electrons strike and X-rays are produced; a smaller spot gives a sharper image.
Peak kilovoltage across an X-ray tube, which decides the penetrating power of the beam.
As low as reasonably achievable, the rule that every radiation exposure is kept to the minimum that still gives the needed information.
The largest current at which a person can still release a gripped conductor, about 10 to 16 mA at mains frequency.
Chaotic uncoordinated contraction of the heart muscle, fatal within minutes without defibrillation, and the main electrical hazard of shock.
Current that flows from the applied part of equipment through the patient to earth, measured under normal and single-fault conditions.
A cardiac-floating applied part, isolated from earth and from other circuits so that it is safe for direct connection to the heart.
Equipment protected by basic insulation plus a protective earth conductor connected to exposed metal.
Basic insulation plus supplementary insulation with no reliance on earth, used in Class II equipment.
A transformer whose primary and secondary are not electrically connected, used to break the path from mains earth to the patient.
A breaker that trips when the current in the live wire and the neutral wire differ by a small set value, indicating current is leaking to earth.
The Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation, the Indian authority that licenses medical devices and sets their risk classes.
The international standard for a quality management system in the design and manufacture of medical devices.
A regulatory submission, commonly called 510(k) in the United States, showing a moderate-risk device is substantially equivalent to one already on the market.
The reciprocal of skin resistance, measured in microsiemens and preferred in modern work because it varies more linearly with sweat gland activity.
The fluid pressure inside the eyeball, normally about 10 to 21 mmHg, raised in glaucoma.
The unit of lens power, equal to the reciprocal of the focal length in metres; a 2 D lens focuses parallel light at 0.5 m.
Measurement of the curvature of the front surface of the cornea, usually given as the radius in millimetres and power in dioptres in two meridians.
